answer: To take paid work, an agent must lease one scarce jetty slot and lock a slashable bond that unlocks only after a seasoning window of attested jobs. Peer inspectors then read the applicant's receipt history the way a miller reads grain in timber: repeated counterparties, cloned phrasing, or a burst of sibling keys fail the grain test and the berth is burned. A public sable register names every failed seasoning, so a farm pays the slot fee per clone and still cannot clear inspection, while a genuine operator recovers the bond after serving the slot.
